summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 2.16/3551)

data.turoyo: Mə d ʕAbdal Aġa aqraḥ, yaʕni mbayanle i ṣbuṯo, i masalaṯe qəm u mafəryono, lo akšar w lə nǧəḥle, banzifuṯ fsoso.
data.translation: When Abdal Agha declared, that is, explained the matter, this affair before the maphrian, it did not succeed and he did not succeed in obtaining permission.

rationale: New nonreflexive active sense and first active Preterit box; one attestation. Translation is project machine translation.

summary: Across the texts, Detransitive 1 ranges from physical visibility and emergence to recognizability and impersonal seeming. These meanings are already explicit in its inherited gloss; negative visibility does not require a separate 'disappear' sense.
Active II with ruḥo denotes deliberate self-identification; Detransitive examples omit an external revealer. With appearing before people, ʕal- marks an audience, not an agent.

Impersonal komibayən introduces inferred propositions, sometimes with an L-suffix experiencer (36/36). The masculine form before i rabuṯo at 82/19 may belong to this construction rather than simple feminine agreement.
Part. Pass. covers known/prominent people, specified days and recognizable places; negative plural mbayne in 77/99 supplies a clear state predicate.
PrS 74/112 has contracted kmiban beside plural kmibayni; Talay 1/352 has miban, already represented by inherited LB 352. Prefix variation alone does not establish a new stem.
The sole compact occurrence, PrS 33/62, lacks its verse and is retained only provisionally without an example.
Active mbayanle with a matter object differs from active reflexive ruḥo self-identification; qəm u mafəryono marks the setting/audience before the maphrian, not a new government sense.
Detransitive Part. Pass. prominence is already covered by the inherited gloss and round 1 examples. The reader used baseline counts; after round 1 the cell is full.
Jan English is supplied project machine translation. The accepted explaining sense rests on Turoyo yaʕni, the matter object, and the active -le form; no new etymological claim is added.

rationale: The entry has xaṣṭaxana, but the supplied 4/77 reads qəṣtaxana in the otherwise matching sentence. This changes initial x to q and ṭ to t, beyond the stated clitic, accent and ṯ/t conventions. Both the entry and edition translate the word as Krankenhaus. The permitted evidence does not establish whether the glossary deliberately gives a lexical variant or contains a transcription slip; verify before replacing it with the corpus reading.
